chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: A righteous servant, peace be upon him, narrated to me.

And I asked him about one performing tamattu' who does not have a sacrificial offering, and the fasting has passed him by until he departs, and he has no stay. He said: He may fast three days on the road if he wishes, and if he wishes he may fast ten among his family.

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّةٌ: a sacrificial offering required in this context
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting allowed on the journey
key_terms.عَشَرَةً: ten days of fasting in total as an alternative completion
key_terms.فِي أَهْلِهِ: after returning to his family or home
key_terms.مُقَامٌ: a period of staying or remaining in a place
key_terms.ٱلصَّوْمُ: the prescribed fasting obligation mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a person performing tamattu' fast the required days while traveling if he missed them before leaving?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the one performing Hajj al-tamattu' who does not have an udhiyah and missed the prescribed fasting before departure. The Imam عليه السلام permits him to fast three days while traveling, or alternatively to fast ten days after returning to his family.
